commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Replace assert with runtime overflow check in expat_realloc

In expat_realloc, the size passed to realloc_fcn is calculated as
sizeof(size_t) + EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING + size. Previously, expat_realloc
relied on an assertion:
assert(SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING >= size);
under the assumption that preceding accounting checks and parser
invariants preclude reaching an overflow state in practice.

However, in release builds compiled with NDEBUG, assertions are
compiled out. Replace the assert with an explicit runtime check:
if (size > SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING) {
  return NULL;
}
immediately preceding the addition, ensuring consistent defensive
behavior across all build configurations.

Also reserve one byte beyond XML_GetBuffer's growth target, so a fully
occupied parser buffer still has storage for a terminator.

Also extend test_alloc_tracker_size_recorded in alloc_tests.c to
exercise SIZE_MAX and SIZE_MAX / 2 with expat_realloc, verifying
that the allocation fails and the recorded size remains unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>

lib|tests: Validate len against buffer capacity in XML_ParseBuffer

In XML_ParseBuffer(), if len exceeds the unoccupied capacity of the
internal buffer (EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferEnd)),
parser->m_bufferEnd was previously advanced past parser->m_bufferLim.
This violated the parser's internal pointer invariant (m_bufferEnd <=
m_bufferLim) and caused callProcessor() to read unallocated or
uninitialized heap memory beyond the buffer bounds.

Validate that len <= EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferEnd) for
both XML_INITIALIZED and XML_PARSING states. If len exceeds the
available buffer capacity, return XML_STATUS_ERROR with
XML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Make replacement-buffer growth strict and trim the resulting
power-of-two margin by one byte.

Also add test_parse_buffer_exceeds_buffer in tests/basic_tests.c.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Pipping <sebastian@pipping.org>
Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>

coupling: The first edited commit introduces a one-byte reservation in XML_GetBuffer's growth target: allocationSize is neededSize minus one, while the actual malloc and m_bufferLim both use bufferSize plus one. The later edited commit changes growth to be strict (bufferSize <= allocationSize) and trims one byte from both the malloc and m_bufferLim (bufferSize minus one). Either change by itself keeps the public XML_GetBuffer(len) contract satisfied: the first over-reserves a byte, and the second relies on the strict growth margin when trimming. Together, the target is one byte below the required size, strict growth can land exactly at the required size, and the trimmed allocation is one byte short. For a 2048-byte request, the combined tree allocates and exposes 2047 bytes, so an in-contract 2048-byte copy into the returned buffer is a heap out-of-bounds write. A correct fix must reconcile the target relaxation in the first commit with the allocation trim in the second; reasoning about only one side of that shared one-byte margin can restore the mismatch rather than the invariant.
